pvmq5tb.s: Upscale cocktail lounge with a rooftop bar at Beekman Tower on Mitchell Place, near the UN.

p1wrvh3s.s: Paul Sevigny's cool-kids hangout inside the Roxy Hotel in Tribeca (first called Paul's Baby Grand), with Palm Beach-on-acid decor.

pjjwc9a.s: Sky-high bar at Peak on the 101st floor of 30 Hudson Yards, which also runs the late-night cocktail spot Peakaboo.

p1iuevz5.s: Swanky '70s-style lounge upstairs from Heroes in SoHo, with wood paneling, black velvet and caviar service, styled after Playboy After Dark.

p18ljy5a.s: Low-key Bushwick bar with drink specials and themed performance and comedy nights.

p1w67a7.s: Lower East Side bar on Orchard Street where owner Katie Rue makes Korean-inspired cocktails with lots of fresh produce.

pcjhegm.s: Greenwich Village sports bar on University Place for game nights, beer and underrated bar food.

pvkl1oq.s: Hell's Kitchen dive on 9th Avenue since 1933, famous for cheap beer and free hot dogs.

p1qy5bi.s: Moody basement bar in the Walker Hotel off Cortlandt Alley in Tribeca. A good second- or third-date spot.

pa7pc05.s: Underground East Village sake bar, open since 1993 and a pioneer of sake, shochu and Japanese whisky in NYC. Look for the "On Air" sign on the stairs.

p1i8b3p.s: Williamsburg wine bar on Bedford Avenue with a killer backyard and staff who help you find exactly what you like.

p17n6y23.s: Legendary basement jazz club on West 10th Street with sets late into the night. Arrive early for the good seats.

p1ci80qn.s: SoHo cocktail bar that feels like a secret clubhouse, good for a date and fancy chicken nuggets.

p16a9uqx.s: Dollhouse-sized all-day cafe and wine bar on West 10th Street, opening around 7:30am. One of the best places in the West Village to read, chat and drink.

pq3sinw.s: Hidden East Village listening bar behind an unmarked door on Avenue C, with late-night sushi and a four-seat omakase counter.

p90963r.s: Fun Mexican-American bar at 1st and 1st with creative cocktails and a great birria grilled cheese.

p123sr7n.s: Fancy cocktail bar from the team behind Estela, in the Nine Orchard hotel on the Lower East Side.

pb444fn.s: Sultry SoHo lounge with jewel-toned velvet couches, antique mirrored columns and weekend DJs.

p4sn6o8.s: Subterranean jazz club under the Roxy Hotel in Tribeca, with vaulted brick ceilings, live jazz, food and cocktails.

pzpj62s.s: Cozy Swiss wine bar and restaurant in the West Village, and one of the best places for fondue in NYC.

p1f0fqtg.s: Velvet-roped Nolita bar and late-night den with inventive cocktails and a fashion crowd. It opened during New York Fashion Week.

p1egtrlz.s: Hotel bar in NoMad where you can sit under a taxidermy ostrich with a date and a few snacks.

p1pbaysv.s: Cocktail bar, lounge and late-night club inside a giant water tower on the roof of the Williamsburg Hotel.

p127m66b.s: Lower East Side dive styled as a '70s rec room, with a pool table, Ms. Pac-Man, plastic-covered couches and cheap drinks.

p10zdqab.s: Two-level East Village bar on Avenue A: a chill bar upstairs and a lively dance floor in the basement.

p1vh8srs.s: Laid-back East Village cocktail bar from the duo behind Barcelona's Two Schmucks, with comfy couches.

p1nwmpxc.s: Three-floor Australian pub in FiDi serving Aussie lager and meat pies. Handy for a big group.

p1ho9w3w.s: Chinatown noodle shop where you watch noodles get hand-pulled, served in chili oil-slicked bowls with dumplings.

p1tmx2fe.s: Clubby West Village steakhouse famous for its prime rib, a hard-to-get reservation with theatrical service.

prq2dyf.s: Smash-burger shop that always draws a crowd. It has grown into a small chain, but the burgers are still worth the wait.

p1njksbh.s: The original East Village location of the smash-burger shop that always draws a crowd on the sidewalk.

p1cfripl.s: Hot pot and Korean barbecue chain, open late, good for a fun group dinner.

p12qe8em.s: Mini outpost of Katz's Delicatessen in DeKalb Market Hall, Downtown Brooklyn, with a short list of the deli's classics.

pww0xkd.s: Retro-feeling Korean restaurant in the East Village specializing in seafood.

pzpu5hw.s: East Village bagel shop from the sourdough-pizza team at Leo, making some of the best craggy sourdough bagels in the city.

p1em6wd5.s: Old-school red-sauce Italian restaurant in Williamsburg, an institution since 1900.

pk3s6ws.s: Boerum Hill Italian restaurant, the second from Stefano Barbagallo and Adriana Luque after their Seaport original.

p2dc6qm.s: Upscale steakhouse a block from Grand Central in the Dylan Hotel, from two Peter Luger alumni.

puaofb3.s: Retro Greenpoint tavern with checkered tablecloths and nostalgic American comfort food.

py29796.s: Classic Chinatown spot on Mott Street for roast duck, congee, noodles and dumplings in a simple room.

p16n80yq.s: Chinatown noodle shop on Bayard Street, an offshoot of the 1986 original, serving pho and other noodle soups.

pdi6u9p.s: Greenwich Village sandwich shop with a long list of good sandwiches and an even longer line.

p1fu56xr.s: Casual Upper West Side Vietnamese restaurant known for excellent bún bò and bánh mì, plus dishes rarely seen elsewhere in the city.

p196drit.s: Michelin-starred Korean steakhouse from restaurateur Simon Kim, blending Korean barbecue with a classic American steakhouse. This is the newer 550 Madison location.

p1r9gufc.s: Bustling Upper East Side Alsatian brasserie with big portions, a popular brunch and a deep beer list.
